pages.text: "I'll just look, then give it back!" By the water in spring, Pongi took her brother's shell in her paws. But it slipped. Plop! It sank into the water. "Oh... what do I do?" Pongi stood still.
Her brother looked into the water, close to tears. "My shell..." Pongi's cheeks felt hot. "I have to say I dropped it..." she thought. But her lips wouldn't open, as if they were stuck together.
Pongi kept her mouth shut and quietly turned toward the bank path. Her brother crouched alone by the water and stared into it. Nobody spoke. The waterfront grew quiet.
Mom, wearing her headscarf, came onto the path. Pongi's mouth drooped. "Your heart feels heavy, Pongi?" Mom sat her on her lap and patted her back. "What could help when you feel that way?"
Pongi gripped her paws together in front of her chest. Keeping quiet made her chest feel tighter and more prickly. "What do I do...?" she said very softly.
Then her brother came quietly over. "Sis..." He held his empty paws out to her. He missed his shell too. Pongi's heart gave a thump.
Pongi clenched both paws beside her body. She took a big breath and looked straight at her brother. "I dropped your shell. I'm sorry!" She thumped her tail. Her brother looked right at her.
After she said it, the tight feeling in her chest slowly grew lighter. Her brother opened his mouth. "It's all right, Sis." They held each other's paws.

They lay side by side at the water's edge. Pongi reached a paw into the water. The shell was right nearby. "One, say right away when you've done something wrong! Two, look at them and say sorry! Three, get it back together!"

Mom hugged them both tight. "Saying sorry was hard, wasn't it?" Once stuck lips open, a heavy heart can slowly feel lighter. Pongi smiled and handed the shell to her brother. "I dropped it. I'm sorry!"
